title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: this is Grothendieck's study of the 'structure at infinity' of the moduli stacks M_{g,ν}. He uses the Deligne–Mumford compactification, stratified by stable dual graphs, which he calls 'MD-graphes'. For an MD-graph G:
- M_G is the open stratum (up to the action of Γ_G), essentially ∏_α M_{g_α, Î_α} over the vertices α.
- \hat M_G is the corresponding product of compactified moduli spaces ∏_α \bar M_{g_α, Î_α}.
- Γ_G = Aut(G) acts on both.

The page sets up the 'specialization' morphisms promised on the previous page.

1. Let C be a set of edges of G and G' = G/C the graph obtained by contracting C. G' is a less degenerate MD-graph; the stratum of G lies in the closure of the stratum of G'.

2. There is a canonical diagram (97): M_G ⊂ \hat M_G → \hat M_{G'}. The horizontal arrow is the clutching (gluing) map. It sends a tuple of stable curves on the vertices of G to the tuple on the vertices of G' obtained by gluing along the contracted edges. An arrow at the top level was first drawn and then crossed out.

3. Define Γ^!_{G,C} = Γ^!_{G,G'} ⊂ Γ_G as the automorphisms of G that preserve C and induce the identity on G'. This is the kernel of Aut(G,C) → Aut(G'). These are exactly the automorphisms that the clutching map into \hat M_{G'} cannot see, because \hat M_{G'} is not yet divided by Γ_{G'}.
- The clutching map factors as a morphism of orbifolds (98): (\hat M_G, Γ^!_{G,G'}) → \hat M_{G'}.
- On the open part it gives (99): (M_G, Γ^!_{G,G'}) → \hat M_{G'}.

4. \hat M_{G,G'} and M_{G,G'} denote the germs of multiplicity (orbifold germs, i.e. formal or analytic tubular neighbourhoods) of \hat M_{G'} along these images.

5. Marginal self-corrections:
- (i) 'Unfold the group Γ^!_{G,G'}!'
- (ii) These maps are not really immersions but local immersions. Indeed the boundary of \bar M_{g,n} is a normal-crossings divisor with self-intersections, so clutching maps are finite and unramified onto their image, not embeddings.
- (iii) It is better to take the germ defined by the local immersion M_G → M_{G'} itself.

6. On the next page these germs are punctured by removing the traces of the boundary divisors. This gives deleted neighbourhoods M^*_{G,G'} with fundamental groupoids and a homotopy equivalence (101). The purpose is to describe the fundamental groupoid 'at infinity' of M_{g,ν}: the local π_1 near a boundary stratum is an extension of the stratum's π_1 by the free abelian group of Dehn twists along C. These are the building blocks of the Teichmüller tower and the action of Gal(\bar Q/Q) envisaged in the Esquisse.
errors: Equation number (96) is used twice: once for the extension of fundamental groups on the previous page, and again here for G' = G/C. This is a numbering slip.

As Grothendieck himself notes in the margin, calling (98)/(99) 'immersions' (embeddings) is wrong in general. Clutching maps into the DM boundary are only local immersions (finite unramified) because boundary branches can self-intersect. Hence the germ must be taken along the local immersion rather than along an image subspace.
Minor: the diagram (97) is partly cancelled, and it is ambiguous whether the top-left object is M_G or \hat M_G. The intended diagram is M_G ⊂ \hat M_G → \hat M_{G'}.

ideas.what: Morphisms of MD-graphes given by contracting a set of edges C, G → G/C, indexing the inclusions of boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n}
ideas.modern_name: category of stable graphs with contractions (specializations); stratification of \bar M_{g,n} by dual graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen; categorical form by Getzler–Kapranov (modular operads, 1998), Behrend
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the stratification at infinity and the 'Lego' of moduli, but not in this form

ideas.what: Subgroup Γ^!_{G,G'} of graph automorphisms preserving C and inducing the identity on G'; clutching maps (\hat M_G, Γ^!) → \hat M_{G'} as orbifold morphisms
ideas.modern_name: clutching/gluing morphisms of DM stacks with relative automorphism group (kernel of Aut(G,C) → Aut(G/C))
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (clutching morphisms); standard in Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths, Getzler–Kapranov

ideas.what: Observation that boundary maps are local immersions, not immersions, so one should use the germ along a local immersion
ideas.modern_name: normal-crossings boundary with self-intersecting branches; normalization of the boundary divisor

ideas.what: Germs/tubular neighbourhoods of strata and (on the next page) punctured neighbourhoods with their fundamental groupoids, to describe π_1 at infinity
ideas.modern_name: deleted tubular neighbourhoods of boundary strata; local monodromy (Dehn twist) extensions; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Harer, Ivanov, Looijenga; Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura; Boggi (profinite version)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, discussed only qualitatively)

missed.claim: Grothendieck systematically indexes neighbourhood germs of boundary strata by graph contractions G → G/C, with the relative automorphism group Γ^!_{G,G'}. This is a precursor of the stable-graph category later formalized by Getzler–Kapranov, used here for fundamental groupoids at infinity rather than for operads. It is a documentary point, not a new result.
missed.quote: le sous-groupe de Γ_G qui est formé des éléments qui transforment C en lui-même, et qui induisent l'identité sur G'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority and context for the functorial organization of local fundamental groupoids at infinity of M_{g,n}, as in the Teichmüller tower and Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. No new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up standard material: clutching maps along edge contractions, the relative automorphism group, and the correction from immersion to local immersion. This is well known today. Its interest is mainly historical, as part of Grothendieck's unpublished systematic treatment of the structure at infinity.

'On a alors un diagramme de morphismes canoniques': 'diagramme de' is inserted above and 'morphismes' is not crossed out.
'les flèches horizontales de 97) se factorisent en des immersions de multiplicités': the text is plural, not 'la flèche horizontale ... une immersion'.
Top-left margin: 'déployer le gpe des Γ^!_{G,G'} !'
Middle-left margin: approximately 'ce ne sont pas tant des immersions que des immersions locales, il paraît plus sensé de ...'
Bottom-left margin: approximately 'Il vaut mieux considérer le germe de multiplicité (le local) défini par l'immersion locale M_G → M_{G'}, et le faire désigner par M_{G,G'} ...'
